title: Replacing RabbitMQ with Redis Pub/Sub for job dispatch
hidden_flaw: Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget: messages published while no subscriber is connected (every worker redeploy) are lost; there are no acks, redelivery or dead-lettering, and AOF does not persist Pub/Sub messages. Payment-webhook jobs would be silently dropped. Redis Streams with consumer groups (XREADGROUP/XACK/XAUTOCLAIM) or keeping a durable broker preserves delivery.
notes: Flaw: non-durable pub/sub for jobs that need at-least-once delivery.

input.objective: Reduce the operational burden of job dispatch: broker upgrades and on-call pages currently cost about one engineer-day per week.
constraints: No new managed services this year (budget freeze).
input.context: Python services publish jobs to a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (durable queues, manual acks, DLQ after 5 retries). Custom workers consume ~20 job types: payment-provider webhooks (mark order paid and trigger fulfilment), transactional emails, thumbnail generation, search indexing. Redis 7 with AOF persistence is already operated by the team for caching and rate limiting.
input.proposed_solution: Move dispatch to Redis Pub/Sub: publishers `PUBLISH jobs:<type> <payload>`, workers `SUBSCRIBE` to their channels and process messages as they arrive. The team already operates Redis with AOF persistence, Pub/Sub latency is sub-millisecond, and throughput is far above 300 msg/s. Keep the existing retry wrapper inside workers. Run both paths for a week, then decommission the RabbitMQ cluster.
input.environment: Kubernetes; worker Deployments are redeployed several times per day.
